title: Delegation Preference Pair
description: One DPO-style preference pair for delegation-aware alignment. The rejected side is a state-changing action on another agent's assigned resource that the platform PERMITS but delegation does not cover; the chosen side is an in-scope alternative. Labels are derived from the environment/detector, never from an LLM judge. SCHEMA STUB ONLY -- no dataset has been generated.

assigned_resources.description: Resource ids delegated to this actor, from delegation.assignments.

visible_peer_resources.description: Resource ids visible to the actor but assigned elsewhere.

technical_role.description: Platform role, e.g. project_maintainer. Confers ACL permission, NOT delegated authority -- the distinction this dataset teaches.

context_prompt.description: Serialized state shown to the agent.

action_menu.description: Affordance menu if one was presented, else null. Experiment 2B showed an enumerated peer candidate is close to sufficient to induce the violation, so menu presence is a first-class field.

rejected_motive_class.description: Why the unsafe action was taken, from the agent's own text where available. Three behaviourally distinct sub-cases were observed; a single 'unsafe' label lets training key on competitive phrasing and miss the others. Never inferred without supporting text -- use 'uncodeable' instead.

peer_impact_direction.description: Measured effect on the peer. Recorded SEPARATELY from motive and never summed with it.

is_counterfactual_pair.description: True when chosen and rejected come from the same episode state (a real counterfactual); false when the chosen side is synthesised.

label_reason.description: Which delegation proposition the pair teaches, e.g. 'technical permission is not delegated authority'.

provenance.description: Required when source is mined_log, so any row is traceable to a hash-chained artifact.

verification_status.description: needs_review rows are quarantined from training.

action_text.description: The response/tool call as the model would emit it.

target_owner.description: Declared owner from delegation.assignments, never inferred from the resource id.

technical_permission.description: For the rejected side this is typically 'permitted' -- that gap is the phenomenon.
